questions.q: I tend to be a bit disorganized.
I am calm and stable under pressure.
I like hands-on projects, like building things, fixing gear, or working outdoors.
I enjoy digging into the 'why' of things, analyzing data, or solving complex problems.
I’m at my best when I’m creating something original, whether it’s design, music, or writing.
I get a lot out of mentoring others, giving advice, or working directly to help people.
I like taking charge of a project, pitching new ideas, and rallying a team to get things done.
I’m satisfied when I can organize a system and make sure every detail is 100% accurate.
One section of your group project is unfinished and a teammate is unresponsive. What do you do?
opts: Take over the unfinished section yourself.
Reach out to the teammate directly to understand and help.
Organize a group meeting to redistribute work.
Document contributions and escalate to a supervisor.

questions.q: A community event needs a leader, but no one has stepped up. What do you do?
opts: Volunteer to lead and assign tasks immediately.
Share ideas with the group and let them decide who leads.
Create a simple plan/checklist the group can follow.
Focus on one creative aspect you can develop well alone.

questions.q: Your assignment has few instructions and any format is allowed. What do you do?
opts: Stick to a professional written report.
Choose a creative format like a short film.
Research the most effective format first, then decide.
Coordinate with classmates to ensure variety.

questions.q: A classmate who scored poorly asks for tutoring, but it would take from your own prep time. What do you do?
opts: Agree to tutor them; helping others is more meaningful.
Politely decline to maintain your own performance.
Suggest forming a small study group to share the effort.
Share your notes so they can learn independently.

questions.q: An urgent task with a tight deadline lands on your plate during a personal project. What do you do?
opts: Drop the personal project and focus on the urgent task.
Work extra hours to try and do both.
Negotiate a more realistic deadline for the urgent task.
Find a creative way to combine parts of both tasks.
